title: Maharashtra FDA Shuts Fortis Hospital Kitchen, Six Domino's Outlets in Crackdown
excerpt: Inspectors reported cockroaches, fungus and rusted knives at the Sodexo kitchen inside Fortis Hospital, Mulund, as the FDA suspended 25 food establishments and four manufacturing units statewide.
body:
• Maharashtra FDA suspended licences of 25 food establishments plus 4 manufacturing units — 29 in total — after inspections found live cockroaches, fungal contamination and unclean utensils.
  • Inspectors at the Sodexo-run kitchen inside Fortis Hospital, Mulund, which cooks for patients, reported cockroaches, food waste near drains, fungus-infested transport containers and rusted knives.
  • Six Domino's Pizza outlets in the Pune division, run by Jubilant FoodWorks, were among those suspended; officials seized 81,330 kg of stock worth Rs 1.73 crore from 37 establishments.
  • Seized samples have gone for laboratory testing; further action under the Food Safety and Standards Act follows the reports, and 10 FIRs were filed in a parallel drive against banned products.

Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration has suspended the licences of 25 food establishments and four manufacturing units in a statewide food-safety crackdown, shutting the kitchen that cooks for patients at a Mumbai hospital and six Domino's Pizza outlets after inspectors reported cockroaches, fungus and rusted equipment.

The lead case is the kitchen inside Fortis Hospital in Mulund, run by Sodexo India Services. Inspectors found cockroaches in the food-preparation area, food waste near drainage, fungus-infested food transport containers and rusted knives, according to reporting on the FDA's October 16 press note. The FDA did not clarify whether food from that kitchen had been served to patients. A hospital kitchen is held to a higher standard than a restaurant because its meals go to people already ill.

How the counts fit together

Reports have cited 19, 25 and 29 establishments. The figures describe different slices of the same action. The FDA suspended 25 food establishments — seven in Mumbai division, eight in Pune, two in Konkan and eight in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar — and separately suspended four edible-oil and spice manufacturing units, making 29 suspensions in total, Livemint reported, citing PTI. Earlier divisional releases counted fewer suspensions because they covered only part of the state.

At the Domino's outlets in Pune, inspectors reported live cockroaches and their remains, incomplete temperature records, inadequate separation of vegetarian and non-vegetarian ingredients, and foul smells from toilets near dining areas. In Mumbai, Janata Bakery in Jogeshwari East scored 28 out of 88 marks on inspection. The Sophia College canteen, Mumbai Bites in Girgaum and Arihant Aahar in Ghatkopar, where a complaint alleged unauthorised artificial colours in sweets, were also named.

Seizures and manufacturing units

Officials seized about 81,330 kg of suspected substandard, adulterated or mislabelled food worth Rs 1.73 crore from 37 establishments across six divisions. The stock included edible oils, chilli and turmeric powders, areca nut, dry fruits, sabudana, bhagar, rajgira, tea powder and sweets. At Pol Agro Industries in Lasur Station, 9,165 kg of refined soybean oil worth about Rs 15.03 lakh was seized after the unit scored 19 out of 86 marks. In Dharmabad, Nanded, three units had 25,768 kg of chilli powder, turmeric powder and edible salt seized, with the FDA saying the products were intended for adulteration.

The FDA said the establishments violated Schedule 4 of the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011, which sets hygiene and sanitary requirements. In a separate October 14-15 drive against banned products, it inspected 13 establishments and vehicles, seized banned stock worth Rs 18.83 lakh plus two vehicles, filed 10 FIRs and sealed four establishments.

What happens next, and what consumers can check

Samples of the seized stock have been sent for laboratory analysis. "Samples of the seized products have been sent for laboratory analysis. Further legal action will be taken under Food Safety and Standards Act after the reports are received," the FDA said. FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe said statewide inspections will continue to stop the sale, storage and transport of banned products.

For consumers, the practical check is the licence itself: every food business in India must display its FSSAI licence or registration number, and a suspended licence means the outlet should not be operating. If a favourite outlet disappears from delivery apps or shutters without explanation during this drive, a suspension is a likely reason — and reopening depends on corrective action and the regulator, not the brand alone.
